_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for LMT retrospectives (retro/build_lmt.py), generated from the converted rows of Lockheed Martin's filings (every figure read from its labelled row, the row asserted present in its own filing). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2006-2009 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend (else the vintage's). Lockheed Martin's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is diluted EPS (from continuing operations where reported), each year from the latest 10-K that reports it; FY2002 is excluded (unusual items larger than its earnings, no per-share figure excluding them), so the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 ('pe_window_start'). A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it; backlog against the year-ago quarter's end as that quarter's own release shows it ('backlog_prior_source'). Guides: the fiscal-year outlook table's 'Current Update' column (net sales and diluted EPS ranges; segment operating profit and cash from operations are display only: no margin is derived from two guided figures), and the third-quarter release's preliminary outlook for the next year. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'.

history_vintages.why: 'In 2006, 84% of our net sales were made to the U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor.' (FY2006 10-K, Item 1); 'Reduced funding for defense procurement and research and development programs could adversely affect our ability to grow or maintain our sales and profitability.' (Item 1A): sales that depend on Congressional appropriations are not earnings that are the cycle, so DURABLE (the CAT and SO precedent); OFFSHORE (live from 2004-11-05) is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, and the 10-K names no offshore competition, so no disruption theme in scope is live

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each annual change from the latest 10-K published by then that tabulates both years, as tabulated. Backlog is total negotiated backlog at year-end and net sales the five-year summaries' (the FY1998-FY2000 10-Ks' backlog charts; seams stay in: discontinued operations restate 1999 and 2000 backlog and net sales in later 10-Ks). Segment operating profit and the segment margin ('Total business segments' operating profit on the table's total net sales) are tabulated on the recast basis of the 8-K of 2003-01-16 (unusual items, the FAS/CAS pension adjustment and stock-based compensation outside the segments) from the FY2002 10-K, so they have 2001-2006 (the AVGO rule): the FY1998-FY2001 10-Ks report segments that include unusual items and pension income, with a Corporate and Other segment, a different measure. EPS is the FY2006 history's (2004-2006: FY2002 is excluded and the history starts with FY2003; the F and SO rule)

price_basis: Yahoo's LMT series is adjusted for the 1995-03-16 factor (1.63, the Lockheed and Martin Marietta combination) and the 2-for-1 split of 1999-01-04; both precede every per-share fact in this file (the history starts with FY2003), so Yahoo's close is the price as traded on every day of every P/E window
